articles.headline: Man United-linked Lewis Hall: 'No-brainer' to stay at Newcastle
articles.description: Lewis Hall has said it was a "no-brainer" to sign a new contract to extend his Newcastle United stay after summer transfer interest from Manchester United.
articles.headlineJa: マンU関心のルイス・ホール、ニューカッスル残留は「迷う余地もなかった」
articles.descriptionJa: ルイス・ホールは、夏の移籍市場でマンチェスター・ユナイテッドからの関心が寄せられたものの、新契約を結んでニューカッスル・ユナイテッドでの滞在を延長することは「迷う余地もない選択」だったと語りました。
articles.body:
Lewis Hall has said it was a "no-brainer" to sign a new contract to extend his Newcastle United stay after summer transfer interest from Manchester United.

Hall, 22, signed a new "long-term" Newcastle deal on Sept. 11, but was Man United's primary target in the left-back position. No official bids were lodged for the England fullback. 

He has showed impressive form for the Magpies since joining them from Chelsea on what was an initial loan deal in 2023 that was made permanent the following year. 

Asked if it felt difficult amid heightened speculation over his future this summer, Hall told Chronicle Live: "No, honestly, it didn't. I guess whenever you're linked to another team, you know that you're doing something right. I guess it's just a credit to your own performances and how you are as a player, how you are as a person.

"I took that as a positive, but at the same time, I knew how much I love playing here and I knew that since the manager came in, I knew the ambitions and what we wanted to achieve.

"After not many conversations, not many training sessions, I knew that the manager was going to be really good for this club and I knew that as a team, bringing in new players and improving the squad was really important and as soon as we did that, it was a no-brainer really to sign."

Hall scored the winning goal as Newcastle beat Hull City 2-1 on Saturday and has been recalled by England after missing out on the World Cup squad.

Man United have struggled to rekindle the form that saw them finish third last season and are 12th during the first international break of the campaign.

- First-month grades for all 20 Premier League teams: A+ to F

Hall, though, did admit he is unsure over his long-term future at Newcastle. Asked if signing a new deal is a signifier of his long-term commitment to the club, Hall replied: "I think so. I think when you're at a team you don't think too far into the future. Obviously, I'm really grateful for the contract that I've received and the trust that I've been given from the board and from the manager and everything like that.

"But I'm just taking it game by game, just trying to do the best I can for this club. We've got ambitions and as long as we achieve these ambitions and achieve what we want to achieve, I'm sure I'll be here for a long time."

Newcastle travel to face Coventry City in their next fixture on Oct. 12.

articles.headline: NBA Rank 2026: 10 players to watch in next season's top 100
articles.description: There's always next year. Ben Golliver and Zach Kram examine 10 players already on our radar for 2027 NBA Rank.
articles.headlineJa: NBAランク2026：来シーズンのトップ100で注目すべき10人の選手
articles.descriptionJa: 挑戦は常に次へと続きます。ベン・ゴリバーとザック・クラムが、2027年NBAランクで早くも注目を集めている10人の選手を分析します。
articles.body:
ESPN's NBA Rank top 100 is underway, with players Nos. 100-51 for the 2026-27 season already unveiled. (The countdown continues Wednesday with Nos. 50-11 and Thursday with our top 10.)

But here, we're focusing on players who missed the cut. Which young stars are on track to make their NBA Rank debut next season? Which veterans are poised for a return? Let's breaking down 10 names to watch for the 2027 countdown, including a reigning Western Conference champion, a former Defensive Player of the Year runner-up and a onetime No. 2 draft pick.

Carter Bryant, San Antonio Spurs

It's easy to lose sight of the 20-year-old Bryant in the Spurs' sea of promising prospects. As a rookie and a 2025 lottery pick, Bryant occupied a minor bench role as a wing defender and played sparingly during San Antonio's memorable playoff run.

But the future looks bright for the 6-foot-6 forward, who fits neatly between franchise center Victor Wembanyama and young guards Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper on the positional depth chart. San Antonio will be thrilled if Bryant can fulfill the classic 3-and-D archetype: He already has the size, strength and quickness to defend multiple positions, and he shot 37% from deep as a freshman at Arizona. The babyfaced Bryant also flashed his athletic tools and charming smile while competing in the 2026 slam dunk contest.

Realistically, a breakthrough might still be a few years away. Bryant was guilty of his fair share of rookie mistakes, and he seems destined to be an afterthought on offense given San Antonio's scoring talent. -- Golliver

Toumani Camara, Portland Trail Blazers

Honestly, Camara should have been included in this year's NBA Rank. The 6-foot-7 forward, who earned 2025 All-Defensive honors, started all 82 games for Portland and averaged a career high in scoring while shooting 37% on 3-pointers in 2025-26.

The most likely explanation for Camara's snubbing: He shot poorly throughout a first-round playoff loss to the Spurs, raising questions about his ability to be a two-way contributor in the postseason. Even so, the 2023 second-round pick has been a major asset for the Blazers, ranking first on the team in minutes, second in points and third in win shares.

Camara, 26, cashed in with a four-year, $82 million contract in 2025 because forwards with his combination of size, length, motor, quickness and the ability to defend multiple positions are hard to find. The fact that he's happy contributing in a low-usage offensive role is just the icing on the cake. -- Golliver

 

Dyson Daniels, Atlanta Hawks

Daniels ranked 55th in NBA Rank 2025, but probably slid off this year's list because his 3-point shooting plummeted from 34% in 2024-25 to 18.8% in 2025-26. Unfortunately, the Hawks' guard had the worst 3-point shooting percentage among all NBA players with at least 100 attempts last season.

articles.headline: Silver linings for MLB's 2026 non-playoff teams
articles.description: Your favorite team won't be playing in October -- but that doesn't mean the season was a total loss. Right?
articles.headlineJa: 2026年MLBプレーオフを逃したチームにとっての「希望の光」
articles.descriptionJa: 応援しているチームが10月にプレーしないとしても、シーズン全体が完全な失敗だったわけではありません。そうですよね？
articles.body:
So your team missed the playoffs. There are worse things, right? Their 2026 MLB season is ending in disappointment, but there are some positives, too. There always are, in every team's campaign, even if they might not always be readily apparent. Not everything has gone wrong.

As the proverb goes, every cloud has a silver lining, a 19th-century saying that has its roots in "Comus", a 1634 poem by John Milton, no relation to Eric. Little known fact, but Milton -- the one who wrote "Paradise Lost" -- wasn't much of a baseball guy.

Some baseball loyalists -- we'll call them "Mets fans" -- tend to fixate on the clouds. Others -- we'll call them "Brooklyn Dodgers fans" -- zero right in on the silver lining and start saying things like, "Wait till next year!"

For teams that have already crossed the mathematical elimination threshold in 2026, the wait for next year begins after the regular-season games are over Sunday. But even those teams head home buoyed by some kind of silver lining, one that hopefully will imbue the looming winter vigil with a hint of anticipation for the inevitable spring to come.

Jump to:

American League | National League

American League

Athletics

Silver lining: Henry Bolte

After a promising start, the Athletics imploded under the dual pressures of injury and underperformance. All of this makes silver-lining hunting more difficult, especially if we don't want to play the "at least they're one year closer to Vegas" card.

Still, Bolte looks like a keeper. He's a walking toolkit with a range of raw skills that includes an MLB-leading sprint speed and 95th percentile bat speed. Despite a raw plate approach that features too much swing and miss, he has still managed a .272/.357/.396 line that for a 22-year-old is bursting with promise.

Add a version of Bolte that improves in his second year to a lineup full of 2026 disappointments ripe for a collective bounce-back, and the Athletics might get back on track quickly, at least on offense. As for the pitching ... we're silver lining people today.

Detroit Tigers

Silver lining: Kevin McGonigle is who we thought he'd be

The Tigers have turned out a few highly rated prospects in recent years, but if you reference prospect ratings for Detroit from four and five years ago, you see a lot of players who have struggled to establish themselves, have gotten hurt, have fallen short or are succeeding for other teams.

On the current roster, Riley Greene remains a cornerstone player, but his rise has been a slow burn. Not so for McGonigle, who entered the season as one of the game's top prospects and has been even better than advertised, right from the very first game.

McGonigle is not only the best rookie in baseball in 2026, he arguably has had the best first season by a Tigers hitter in more than a century. Sometimes hype isn't just hype.

Kansas City Royals

Silver lining: Carter Jensen and Jac Caglianone established themselves as regulars

articles.headline: The Passans: 2026 MLB season awards, with a twist
articles.description: Forget the MVP and Cy Young Award races -- it's time to hand out our annual wide-ranging hardware.
articles.headlineJa: パッサンによる2026年MLBシーズン賞：一味違う視点から
articles.descriptionJa: MVPやサイ・ヤング賞の争いは一度忘れて、年に一度の独自の各種アワードを発表する時が来ました。
articles.body:
While Major League Baseball's awards season doesn't officially arrive until November, that's no reason to wait to pay homage to the best of 2026. These aren't your typical honors, but seeing as how the Baseball Writers' Association of America now hands out 10 awards a year -- MVP, Cy Young, Rookie of the Year, Manager of the Year and the new Reliever of the Year in each league -- here are 10 others to accompany those.

Best Prime Mike Trout Impression: Pete Crow-Armstrong

The Chicago Cubs' star center fielder is not just the National League MVP. He should win the award unanimously. He has been by far the best player in baseball this season, which is saying something in a year in which Shohei Ohtani hit and pitched. What's most impressive, in fact, is the chasm in production between Crow-Amstrong and every other big leaguer.

Only three times in MLB history has the gap between the player with the most FanGraphs wins above replacement and the second-highest WAR total been as large as it is between Crow-Armstrong and Kansas City shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. this season. Crow-Armstrong is sporting an advantage of 3.6 WAR -- 10.2 to 6.6. The other seasons: Babe Ruth over Harry Heilman by 5.7 WAR in 1923, Ruth over Lou Gehrig by 4.8 in 1926, and Mickey Mantle over Duke Snider by 4.0 in 1956.

So, PCA is having the most dominant season, compared with his peers, in seven decades? Well, by one measure, sure. The other major publicly available WAR, Baseball-Reference, has a 1.9-win gap between Crow-Armstrong and Philadelphia ace Cristopher Sánchez -- a top-20 difference in the live ball era but by no means the same sort of edge FanGraphs sees.

And that's fine. Systems can differ in their calculations of value. It doesn't take anything away from the full PCA experience this season. He leads MLB with 45 home runs. He's on top in defensive outs above average, too. He's fifth with 38 stolen bases. He has more than doubled his career walk rate to 11.1%. He has power, defensive chops, speed and patience, and he's having the sort of season only the game's most renowned names put up.

One look at 10-win seasons by outfielders in the past half-century illustrates that. Only five players have reached that mark: Barry Bonds five times, Aaron Judge three, Mike Trout two, and Rickey Henderson, Mookie Betts and Crow-Armstrong one time apiece. None went 40/40 like Crow-Armstrong will look to do with two more stolen bases this week. The closest facsimiles are Trout in his first full season (30 home runs and 49 stolen bases) and Betts in 2018 (32 and 30).

Even though Trout and Betts had better all-around offensive numbers, Crow-Armstrong's acumen at such an important defensive position makes up for whatever offensive deficiencies one chooses to use against him. And given that he has the highest wOBA in the NL this year, Crow-Armstrong's bat has done sufficient talking already.

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: Sleepers, breakouts and busts for 2026-27
articles.description: Which fantasy basketball players are going to exceed expectations in 2026-27? Who will disappoint? Who is ready to take things to an elite level? Our experts list their picks.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジーバスケットボール：2026-27シーズンのスリーパー、ブレイクアウト、バスト候補
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-27シーズンに期待以上の活躍を見せるファンタジーバスケットボール選手は誰か？失望させるのは誰か？トップレベルへ飛躍する準備ができているのは誰か？専門家が注目選手を挙げます。
articles.body:
Putting together a winning fantasy basketball roster starts with a great draft. And to have a great draft, you need to know which players to go after and which to avoid.

So which players will out-produce their average draft position (ADP) this season? Who will take their game to another level? And which players are the biggest risk to take a step backward?

Our fantasy basketball experts André Snellings, Eric Moody, Eric Karabell, Jim McCormick, Steve Alexander and Michael F. Florio offer their top sleepers, breakouts and busts for the 2026-27 NBA season.

Sleepers

Sleeper: A player who will far surpass his average draft position (ADP) in standard ESPN leagues.

Naz Reid, C/PF, Charlotte Hornets

Snellings: Reid was the NBA Sixth Man of the Year two seasons ago and had carved out a role with the Timberwolves as essentially a starter that had to come off the bench due to the depth of frontline talent in Minnesota. With his trade to the Hornets, Reid has the opportunity to show that he can produce even more as a full-time starter. Reid is an efficient scorer, a strong rebounder and defender, and one of the best 3-point shooting big men in the league. Particularly in category leagues, he is poised to return fantasy value far beyond where is selected in most drafts.

Alexander: Reid has always been one of my favorite under-the-radar players and he'll have new life this season, hopefully starting for the Hornets. I wish he was a better free throw shooter (72.8% for his career), but he only shot 1.6 of them per game last year, meaning the low volume won't hurt you too bad in that category. I expect all of his numbers to get a boost this year and he's played between 68 and 81 games in six straight seasons. The only concern is his usage rate while playing alongside Coby White, Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller, but there should be enough to go around for Reid to eat.

Julius Randle, PF, Brooklyn Nets

Karabell: Randle's numbers and fantasy value fell quite a bit during two seasons with the Timberwolves, especially in rebounds, but there is little holding him back from high usage and big fantasy value with the barren Nets. Look at what Randle achieved statistically during his Knicks seasons, and expect a return to at least 24 PPG, 10 RPG and 5 APG for the other New York team, easily outproducing his tepid ADP, which always seemed out of line with his actual production.

Caleb Wilson, SF, Chicago Bulls

Florio: The No. 4 overall pick in this years NBA draft hit the ground running this summer. Wilson averaged 23.5 points, 7.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 2.5 blocks per game in the Summer League. That is after putting up similar numbers at North Carolina last year. He has apparently been turning heads in workouts with LeBron James, too. He will start at power forward on a Bulls team that has lots of opportunities up for grabs, both in terms of scoring and rebounding.
